accepted.reason: EIP-1153 TLOAD/TSTORE of the Lock holder at the fixed ERC-7201 slot LockSlot.HOLDER_SLOT (REQ-LOCK-002). Solidity 0.8.28 transient state variables cannot be placed at a chosen slot, so one opcode of assembly per access is required; each block is memory-safe, reads or writes one word and has no other effect. Covered by TEST-060, PROP-037 (Halmos, Certora) and LockProperties.

Expiry is defined on block.timestamp (SPEC-GOV-013: expired iff block.timestamp >= readyAt + GRACE_PERIOD, 14 days). A validator's few-second timestamp drift cannot matter against a 14-day window; the comparison is the specified rule. Covered by TEST-194, TEST-212, PROP-058 (Halmos).
ERC-7201 namespaced storage: one `$.slot := _STORAGE_SLOT` with a compile-time constant slot (REQ-PSTORE-001), the OpenZeppelin 5 pattern; no other assembly.

Two staticcalls: the store's own getOracleConfig view and LPOracle.checkConfig, passing the returned bytes unchanged (the return encoding of getOracleConfig(address) equals the argument encoding of checkConfig(OracleConfig)), which keeps the OracleConfig codec out of the size-limited setter contracts. Both are STATICCALL; a failed or malformed call counts as every check failing (OracleConfigRejected with 2^256-1), so it fails closed (REQ-PSTORE-009). Covered by TEST-064 (tightenRerunsCheckConfig), TEST-250.

Loosening spacing is defined on block.timestamp (REQ-PSTORE-017, SPEC-GOV-011: block.timestamp >= lastLoosenedAt + normalDelay); a few seconds of drift cannot matter against a 4-5 day spacing. Covered by TEST-225, TEST-063.
Only answer and startedAt of latestRoundData are part of the sequencer-feed check (REQ-PSTORE-023); roundId, updatedAt and answeredInRound are not.
Only observationCardinality of slot0 is compared with twapMinObservations (REQ-PSTORE-027); price, tick and index are not used.
Setters return nothing, so the delegatecall's return data is empty by construction; Address.functionDelegateCall already bubbles any revert.

View calls in loops over the MarketRegistry's markets and a token's routes, made when a governance setter re-checks every affected LPOracle (REQ-PSTORE-009, REQ-CONFIG-024) or in getOracleConfig. All are STATICCALL to registry, LPOracle and integration views; the loop length is the registry's size, which only timelock operations grow, and a reverting callee only makes the governance call revert (fail closed).

View calls in loops over the MarketRegistry's Spokes, markets and debt reserves for the liveness re-check (REQ-PSTORE-021, setMaxFlashFeeBps raise) and the debt-reserve scan (REQ-PSTORE-016, REQ-CONFIG-050). STATICCALL only, at execution of a governance setter or in a view; a reverting callee makes the setter revert (fail closed) and the liveness view return false.

The bounds are constants of the shared ParameterStoreStorage base; each of the six contracts that inherits it (the ParameterStore and its five logic contracts) uses only the bounds of its own setters, so every constant is unused in some of them. Constants occupy no storage.
getOracleConfig reads each pool token's routes in force from the MarketRegistry in a loop over the market's tokens (at most MAX_POOL_TOKENS = 8), view calls only (REQ-CONFIG-072).

The `from` of safeTransferFrom is the immutable LP_VAULT_SWAP, not a caller-chosen address, and deposit reverts NotLPVaultSwap unless msg.sender == LP_VAULT_SWAP (REQ-ESCROW-002), so the escrow only ever pulls from the caller itself, the exact amount that caller approved for this call (REQ-ESCROW-003, REQ-SWAP-076). No third party's allowance can be spent. Covered by TEST-179 (depositOnlyFromLpVaultSwap fuzz), PROP-037 (Halmos, Certora).

The proxy's one entry point forwards the AaveAdapter's calldata to the Adapter's target with no ETH (REQ-PROXY-007); a typed call cannot carry arbitrary calldata. Guarded by msg.sender == ADAPTER and a target with code that is not the proxy; an empty revert becomes CallFailed(target), revert data passes through unchanged and success returns the data (OpenZeppelin Address.verifyCallResult). Covered by TEST-187, TEST-032, PROP-010 and PROP-056 (Halmos, Certora).

The flagged literal is the compiler-embedded `type(PositionProxy).creationCode` bytes, not a numeric constant written in source; hashing it gives PROXY_CREATION_CODE_HASH (REQ-PROXY-085). Covered by TEST-190.
Same as the constructor: the literal is `type(PositionProxy).creationCode`, the init-code prefix of REQ-PROXY-052, not a numeric constant. Covered by TEST-190, PROP-064, PROP-076.

The 'literal' is the compiled VaultToken creation code from type(VaultToken).creationCode, which Slither prints as a hex constant; there is no hand-written numeric literal on the line. The creation code is the audited VaultToken (2.4) and the CREATE3 init code is bytes.concat(creationCode, abi.encode(bindings)) per REQ-VTOKEN-022. Covered by TEST-024 (bindings and predicted address of every deployed token).

The withdrawal delay is defined on block.timestamp (SPEC-FLR-003: executable iff block.timestamp >= executableAt = requestTime + RESERVE_WITHDRAWAL_DELAY, 14 days). A validator's few-second timestamp drift cannot matter against a 1,209,600-second delay; the comparison is the specified rule. Covered by TEST-288 withdrawalWaitsFourteenDays (one second before and at executableAt) and CoverageSpokeProperties.execute.

FlashLoanServed reports the premium the Aave V3 Pool charged, which the source learns only in the Pool's executeOperation callback, so the event follows the Pool's flashLoan call by construction (REQ-FLASH-001). Only LP_VAULT_SWAP may call flashLoan, a nested flashLoan reverts FlashLoanActive (transient context), and executeOperation runs only from the Pool for the open context, so no reentrant call can emit a second or reordered log. Covered by TEST-046 (reentrantLoanRefused, reentrantCallbackRefused), TEST-052 (premiumWithinCapIsRepaid checks the event), PROP-036 and PROP-080 (Halmos, Certora).

Only the answer of latestRoundData is used: the raw-price bound (REQ-CONFIG-035) is a listing-time magnitude check, not a price read, so round id and timestamps are irrelevant; freshness is enforced by the LPOracle. Covered by TEST-139.

MarketRegistered is emitted after the integration's bindMarket (the registered, immutable LPVault, callable only by this registry) and the RiskModule's view drift check; reaching listCollateralMarket again needs APPLICATION_ADMIN (the timelock), so no re-entry can reorder the event. Covered by TEST-138.

Route accounting is by balance deltas over the swap call, never by an external contract's return value: inRecv, each leg's output and every residue are rises of the route's own balances, and the output is LPVaultSwap's balance rise in TOKEN_OUT (REQ-ROUTE-008, REQ-ROUTE-009, REQ-ROUTE-014, REQ-ROUTE-015). Delegatecall dispatch of the router (call site LPVaultSwap._delegate): the target is one of the three immutable logic contracts checked at construction (logicConfig kind and immutables hash, InvalidLogic); selector and arguments are the caller's calldata copied unchanged; on failure the revert data is bubbled unchanged, on success the return data is returned unchanged whatever its length (short, long or oversized responses pass through as the logic contract produced them). Each logic body reverts NotDelegated unless reached through the proxy. Covered by LPVaultSwap.Admin, LPVaultSwap.Admin.fuzz (testFuzz_TEST_242_logicBodiesNeedTheProxy) and every liquidate, settlePending and deleverage test.

Gas-limited payout transfer (call site LPVaultSwapSettlement._deliver, REQ-SWAP-076): the target is the debt asset or a pool token of the settlement, selector transfer(address,uint256), 100,000 gas after a check that 111,588 gas remain, no return data copied (out size 0), so a short, long or oversized response costs no gas and cannot revert; the success flag and return data are ignored by design: the amount that left LPVaultSwap is measured as its own balance fall and amount - sent is escrowed for the recipient in PayoutEscrow. Covered by LPVaultSwap.PayoutEscrow (blocklisted, gas burner, under-delivery, insufficient gas) and LPVaultSwap.Delivery.fuzz.

Balance-delta measurement by design (REQ-PROXY-013, Q-124, Q-271): the step reads the proxy's balance, makes the one Spoke or token call it measures and reads it again; every amount it forwards or checks is that delta, never an absolute balance, so a donation or a balance change by a callee can only fail the step's equality check, never move value. The call runs under the Adapter's Lock (REQ-PROXY-048) and only the Adapter can make the proxy act. Covered by TEST-027 (donatedDustIgnored, shortDeliveryReverts), TEST-029 (donationIgnored, pullDeliveringNothingReverts), TEST-010, TEST-018 and AaveAdapter.Failures.
